name: @w6w-apps/adalo
description: Read and write records in an Adalo app's Collections via the Adalo Collections API.

w6w.longDescription:
Adalo is a no-code app builder whose apps each carry their own built-in database, organized into Collections (roughly: tables) of Records (rows). This app talks to the Collections API that every Adalo app on the Team or Business plan exposes at a fixed host — listing, reading, creating, updating and deleting records inside a named Collection.

Because every Adalo app defines its own Collections and fields, the shapes here stay generic: a Collection ID and a JSON object of field slug → value, rather than a fixed field list, so this app works against any Adalo application without per-schema code. Adalo does not publish an endpoint that enumerates an app's Collections or their field schemas — those are only visible from the app's own generated API Documentation panel in the Adalo builder (Collection menu → API Documentation) — so a workflow author copies the App ID, Collection ID and API key from there once and supplies the Collection ID on every action.

Left out on purpose: listing Collections (no such endpoint exists) and the separate Notifications API (a differently-shaped, non-collection endpoint for pushing a notification to one user, out of scope for this Collections-focused app).
